study_identification_part.si4_title: A generalizable normative deep autoencoder for brain morphological anomaly detection: application to the multi-site StratiBip dataset on bipolar disorder in an external validation framework

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Develop and externally validate a generalizable multivariate normative modeling framework using a deep autoencoder to characterize brain morphological deviations in bipolar disorder, integrating confounder removal and multi-site harmonization.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Harmonization pipeline: concatenate StratiBip HC with HCP-YA, estimate additive/multiplicative site effects via EB (M-ComBat), harmonize all StratiBip (HC+BD) to HCP reference; preserve age, sex, and TIV (for volumes). Validation via Kruskal–Wallis and site classification before/after; post-harmonization no site differences among HCs.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Per-feature Reconstruction Error (RE); Mean Deviation Score (MDS = mean squared error across features); modified z-scores (mZ) with 99th-percentile abnormality threshold; block maxima for extreme deviations; heterogeneity indices; ROC AUC for discrimination

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-level BD vs HC comparisons using one-tailed Mann–Whitney U on feature-wise RE with Cliff's delta and bootstrap CIs; mass-univariate two-tailed MWU on corrected features with BH-FDR; pairwise heterogeneity analysis (mean absolute RE differences); extreme value analysis via block maxima; ROC analysis on MDS with AUC and optimal threshold determination; spatial overlap analysis via Overlap Coefficient and Jaccard on binarized abnormal maps.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: BD shows higher and more heterogeneous deviations than HC with increased extreme values; significant deviations localize notably to basal ganglia, hippocampus, and adjacent regions; individualized mZ-based maps show higher abnormality occurrences but lower spatial overlap in BD.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Training on HCP-YA and external application to 7-site StratiBip showed elevated MDS in BD relative to HC and significant feature-wise RE increases in BD by MWU with effect sizes confirmed by bootstrap CIs. Post-harmonization, site effects among HCs were removed (p > 0.680). Heterogeneity analyses indicated greater within-BD dispersion of RE patterns, and block maxima analyses highlighted heavier tails in BD. Personalized mZ maps (99th-percentile thresholds per feature based on HCP-YA RE distributions) revealed more frequent abnormalities in BD with reduced overlap across subjects. Regionally, deviations concentrated in basal ganglia and hippocampal/adjacent structures, consistent with group-level findings.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Code is available (GitHub) with demo applying trained model to exemplar HCP-YA data; harmonization implemented as sklearn-compatible pipeline enabling EV workflows.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: External validation restricted to young adults (22–37 years); reliance on harmonization using only HC portion to estimate site effects; absence of an independent same-domain (HCP) held-out test set beyond cross-validation; quantitative QC exclusions not detailed in main text (likely in Supplementary).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Data availability: HCP-YA public on ConnectomeDB; StratiBip access restricted. Code availability: https://github.com/inesws/Normative_AE and neuro-combat_pyClasse for harmonization.
